title: Status and Incident Voice Templates — Pocket Guide
content:
Purpose:
This pocket guide collects short, high-utility templates and an internal checklist for incident communications. It’s intentionally compact — copy/paste ready for status pages, customer emails, and war-room note-taking. Use in fast-moving incidents where clarity and consistency matter more than prose.

Scope and audience:
- Primary: on-call SREs, incident leads, and support engineers who write public-facing updates.
- Secondary: product and CS owners who may need to review customer-facing text quickly.

How to use this doc:
- Choose template matching severity (P0/P1/P2).
- Fill required fields ({{incident_id}}, {{start_time}}, {{affected_regions}}, {{estimated_repair}}).
- Post short updates on status.redwood.ai/status and mirror into the incident Slack channel #ops-incident-{{incident_id}}.

Incident severity quick mapping (for comms tone):
- P0 (Severe outage): Broad impact, many customers, immediate mitigation underway. Tone: urgent, factual, frequent cadence (every 15–30m).
- P1 (Major degradation): Significant subset of customers affected. Tone: concerned, informative, cadence every 30–60m.
- P2 (Partial/limited impact): Low-traffic or single-feature impact. Tone: measured, less frequent cadence (1–4 hours).

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners):
- Incident Lead: owns content approval and cadence.
- Communications Lead: edits for clarity and posts to status page/support channels.
- Support Lead: surfaces affected customer list and escalates VIPs.
- Engineering Lead: provides technical summary and ETA.

Internal war-room checklist (first 15 minutes) — quick bullets to mark off:
- Create incident channel: #ops-incident-{{incident_id}} and invite Product/CS owners.
- Set incident doc (confluence/Jira) and link in channel.
- Capture initial facts: start_time, systems impacted, first detection, initial mitigation steps.
- Assign roles above.
- Post initial status page message (Initial template below).
- Notify support to triage VIP customers and prepare CS template.
- Enable rotation/hand-off notes: set next update owner and time.

Status page templates (concise, one-paragraph updates). Replace placeholders before posting. Keep each update <= 3–4 short sentences.

1) Initial / Acknowledged (use within <15m of detection)
Subject: Investigating — partial degradation of API ({{incident_id}})
Body: We are investigating reports of increased errors for the Redwood API affecting generation requests in {{affected_regions}}. Our engineers have identified the issue and are actively investigating. No workaround is available yet; we will provide an update by {{next_update_time}}.

2) Investigating — more detail (follow-up)
Subject: Investigating — root area identified ({{incident_id}})
Body: Update: our investigation indicates the issue is related to the inference pool routing layer causing elevated latency and 5xx errors for requests matching the heavy-seq path. We are running focused diagnostics and attempting a traffic reroute for impacted clusters. Estimated next update: {{next_update_time}}.

3) Mitigating / Partial Fix
Subject: Partial mitigation in progress — traffic reroute applied ({{incident_id}})
Body: We have applied a traffic reroute for the affected GPU cluster which has reduced error rates for most requests. Some users may still experience intermittent failures while we validate cache warm-up. Engineers are monitoring KPIs and will confirm full recovery in the next update.

4) Resolved
Subject: Resolved — service back to normal ({{incident_id}})
Body: The underlying issue has been resolved and normal service has been restored. Root cause: misconfigured kernel selection when a specific model variant scaled rapidly; fix: revert of last deployment + configuration guard. We will post a full postmortem in {{postmortem_location}} when ready.

5) Major outage short-form (for broad, direct impact)
Subject: Outage — generation API degraded across regions ({{incident_id}})
Body: We are aware of a major outage impacting the Generation API across multiple regions. Our engineers are responding and working to re-route traffic. We will share additional updates every 15–30 minutes; next: {{next_update_time}}.

Customer communication templates (email / in-app banner). Use plain language, avoid internal jargon. Keep the first paragraph focused on impact and remediation.

Customer email — short (VIP, P0)
Subject: Incident {{incident_id}} — Update on Generation API outage
Body: Hello {{customer_name}},

We’re contacting you about an incident affecting generation requests for your workloads since {{start_time}}. Some requests returned errors or experienced high latency. Our team has implemented a partial mitigation (traffic reroute) which has restored service for most traffic; you may see intermittent failures for a short period. We are continuing work to fully resolve and will follow up with a timeline and postmortem. If you are experiencing critical business impact, please reply or open a priority ticket referencing {{incident_id}}.

Thank you for your patience,
Maya Lin, Redwood Site Reliability

Customer email — follow-up (post-resolution)
Subject: Incident {{incident_id}} — Resolved and next steps
Body: Hello {{customer_name}},

The incident impacting generation has been resolved as of {{resolved_time}}. We identified a configuration regression triggered by an autoscaling event and reverted the change to restore normal behavior. We will publish a detailed postmortem at {{postmortem_location}} within 72 hours. If you saw any lost jobs or degraded outputs, please let us know and we will prioritize remediation.

Support micro-snippets (for replies in support threads)
- Acknowledgement: "Thanks — we’re investigating. I’ll update you by {{next_update_time}}."
- Workaround available: "There is a temporary reroute; please retry in 5 minutes or use the fallback model alias `model-medium` until full recovery."
- Escalation: "I’ve escalated this to engineering; your case is priority and we’ll follow up within 30 minutes."

Voice & tone rules (short):
- Be human: empathy + facts. Start with what customers see, then what we’re doing.
- No internal acronyms in public messages (e.g., avoid saying: "kv-cache warmup").
- Use times in UTC and include timezone label.
- When uncertain, promise frequency not specifics: "we’ll update every 30 minutes" vs. guessing an ETA.

Internal incident messaging — templated slack post (war-room)
Title: [INVESTIGATING] {{incident_id}} — {{short-impact}}
Body: Summary: {{one-line technical summary}}
Detected: {{start_time}} UTC
Scope: {{affected_services}} / {{percent_of_traffic}}
Impact: customer-facing errors / elevated latencies
Action: immediate mitigation task list: 1) pause deployment X, 2) reroute cluster Y, 3) increase autoscale cap
Owner: {{incident_lead}}
Next update: {{next_update_time}}

Post-incident checklist (to be completed before postmortem)
- Capture timeline with exact timestamps (detection, mitigation, resolution).
- Preserve any relevant logs and core dumps (archive S3 path).
- Identify root cause hypothesis and confirm with data.
- List corrective action items and owners with deadlines.
- Draft customer-facing postmortem paragraph (to be reviewed by Legal/PR if P0).

Fast handover template (for next shift)
- Current status: 
- What’s blocked: 
- Next actions assigned: 
- Suggested owner for next update: 

Short FAQ (for CS/sales use)
Q: Will we be charged for failed requests?
A: We will review account impacts case-by-case. For systemic failures, CS will coordinate credits or adjustments per policy.

Q: Should customers retry?
A: Yes, retry with backoff. If using model-specific aliases, switching to the fallback alias can reduce failures until full recovery.

Quick sending checklist (before posting any public update)
- Confirm {{incident_id}} matches incident channel and Jira.
- Spell-check and remove internal acronyms.
- Ensure next_update_time is set and owner assigned.
- Tag the update with severity and region (for routing to partners).
- If VIPs affected, notify Support lead before public post.

Notes and rationale (why compact templates matter):
In high-pressure incidents long prose slows decisions. Short, repeatable templates reduce miscommunication and help downstream teams automate routing/alerts from status page updates. Keep edits surgical — change only the fields in double braces.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Maya L.)
- 2025-11-15: minor edits and expanded customer snippets (Ethan M.)

End of pocket guide.
